subject: Urgent: FintechCo production timeouts - VPC peering / NAT suspected
messages:
From: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@fintechco.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: oncall@fintechco.com; solutions@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts from our Dedicated cluster

Hi Sean,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood Dedicated endpoint behind our VPC peering starting ~08:40 PDT. Latency jumps, and many client SDKs are hitting connection timeouts; we're getting cascading retries on our side which looks like a retry storm. This began right after we rolled a minor NAT gateway config change (vendor-side) but correlation is not confirmed.

Impact: our payment processing queue backs up; throughput drops ~60% and our customers are reporting failed checkouts. I attached a short pcap and some sample logs. Can you confirm if you see elevated 5xx/429s from Redwood's side and whether there's any change in peering behavior or DNS resolution?

--
Alan Reyes
SRE Manager, FintechCo
alan.reyes@fintechco.com
(Attachment: customer-pcap-20260812.pcap, redwood-sample-logs.txt)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@fintechco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts from our Dedicated cluster

Alan — thanks for flagging, and sorry for the disruption. We are seeing increased 5xx/429 rates on the Dedicated pool servicing your account starting at 08:37 PDT; initial dashboards show a sharp rise in connection resets and long tail latencies consistent with backend timeouts.

I've looped in Monica (CS lead) and Dylan (SRE) to coordinate. Dylan — can you run fast checks on peering/session counts, NAT conntrack, and our ingress LB health? Monica — I'll keep FintechCo updated and coordinate any credit/exec asks if this escalates.

Next: Dylan will share what he finds; we'll publish an initial timeline in 30 minutes.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood-logs-20260812.zip)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts from our Dedicated cluster

Quick triage notes (observed):
- 08:36:57 PDT - sudden jump in upstream 504s from the model-serving tier, concurrent with a big increase in TCP RST from the customer-facing peering IPs.
- NAT conntrack tables on the peering egress nodes show saturation and high churn; ephemeral port exhaustion is plausible.
- DNS lookups from our side for the customer's collector endpoint spiked (many retries visible) — suspicious for a retry amplification.
- Firewall logs show intermittent "session timed out" entries; I suspect idle timeout settings on the customer's NAT or their cloud provider were recently lowered.

Immediate mitigations we tried:
- Increased conntrack limits on the affected egress nodes (partial relief).
- Short-term rate limiting on inbound API tokens from FintechCo to throttle request retries (reduced 429s).
- Opened ticket with cloud NAT vendor for conntrack metrics and looked for asymmetric SNAT behavior.

Next steps being executed:
1) Full packet capture analysis (attached pcap from customer + our internal trace) to validate retransmit patterns.
2) Recommend FintechCo increase NAT ephemeral port pool and idle timeout on their side; Monica, can you coordinate asking them to reverse the recent NAT change for an A/B test?
3) We'll deploy an emergency fallback to route FintechCo traffic via our alternate peering region if conntrack remains saturated (needs ~20 minutes to flip safely).

I'll update in 20 minutes with a status. Evelyn, FYI in case we need to invoke Dedicated runbook for cross-region failover.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: nat-metrics-snapshot.json)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@fintechco.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts from our Dedicated cluster

Alan — thank you for the quick pcap and logs. We're proposing a brief A/B rollback of the NAT configuration on your side to validate if that reduces the retry amplification. If you can revert the change for a 15-minute window that would help isolate.

Separately, to limit customer impact while we diagnose:
- We'll enable short-term client-side throttling guidance (reduce retry attempts to 2 with exponential backoff).
- Redwood will provision an alternate peering route and warm the path — we'll only flip if conntrack doesn't stabilize.

Marissa — looped you in since the impact is severe and FintechCo is a high-value customer; they may request credits and an exec update.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@fintechco.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts from our Dedicated cluster — status and next steps

Alan — final update after 30 hours of remediation & validation:
- Root cause: correlated to a vendor-side NAT config change that reduced TCP idle timeout and reduced ephemeral port allocation on the egress path for the FintechCo peering. That caused connection churn and SNAT collisions on our egress nodes which manifested as 5xx/504 and many client-side 429s during heavy bursts.
- What we did: increased conntrack limits; applied targeted rate-limiting to dampen the retry storm; coordinated rollback of the NAT change with FintechCo vendor; warmed an alternate peering path and failed over traffic for ~45 minutes while the vendor remediated their config.
- Impact: throughput returned to baseline after the vendor rollback + our temporary rate limits; we observed a 92% reduction in 5xx events during the post-fix window.
- Follow-ups (owners/ETA):
  * Dylan - hardened conntrack autoscaling and alerts (ETA 2026-08-18).
  * Evelyn/Eng Ops - add peering healthcheck and automatic fallback on SNAT saturation (ETA 2026-09-01).
  * Monica/CS - schedule 1:1 exec review with FintechCo to present timeline and credit proposal (ETA 2026-08-14).

Attached are the merged logs and the packet-capture summary. We'll also draft the exec one-pager Marissa requested. Apologies again for the impact; we appreciate FintechCo's collaboration during the troubleshooting.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
(Attachments: redwood-logs-20260812.zip, nat-metrics-snapshot.json, customer-pcap-20260812.pcap)
